title: Products Ordered by Every Customer
description:
Find all products that have been ordered by **every single customer** (relational division). A product qualifies only if every customer in the customers table has at least one order for it.

**Table: customers** — `customer_id`, `customer_name`

**Table: orders** — `order_id`, `customer_id`, `product_id`, `product_name`

Output columns: `product_id`, `product_name`. Order by `product_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INTEGER, customer_name VARCHAR); CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, product_name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice'),(2,'Bob'),(3,'Charlie'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,1,'Widget A'),(2,1,2,'Gadget B'),(3,1,3,'Doohickey C'),(4,2,1,'Widget A'),(5,2,2,'Gadget B'),(6,2,4,'Thingamajig D'),(7,3,1,'Widget A'),(8,3,2,'Gadget B');
solution_sql: WITH total_customers AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total FROM customers) SELECT product_id, product_name FROM orders GROUP BY product_id, product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) = (SELECT total FROM total_customers) ORDER BY product_id;

test_cases.description: Widget A (product 1) and Gadget B (product 2) are ordered by all 3 customers; others are not

hints: Count the total number of distinct customers in a CTE or subquery.
GROUP BY product and use HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) = total_customers.
This is the relational division pattern — a product 'passes' only when its distinct customer count equals the full customer count.
explanation: There are 3 customers total. Widget A was ordered by customers 1, 2, and 3 (COUNT DISTINCT = 3 ✓). Gadget B was ordered by customers 1, 2, and 3 (✓). Doohickey C was ordered only by customer 1 (✗). Thingamajig D only by customer 2 (✗). The HAVING clause retains only products matching the total customer count.
